highlights.title: Whatever AI Safety Is, It’s Not This
highlights.summary: Asking AI companies to self-regulate is a great way to pretend like you’ve accomplished something.
body: Here’s a fun history lesson for you. Don’t worry, we’ll make it quick! In 1966, nearly 51,000 people died on US highways. The overwhelming evidence suggested that many lives could have been saved with modern seat belts, which by then had been around for several years. The automotive industry responded by rallying together, and, in a triumph of self-regulation, voluntarily put the safety feature in every new vehicle that rolled off the line.

Kidding! Of course they didn’t do that. In the fall of 1966, Congress established the Department of Transportation and then passed the National Traffic and Motor Vehicle Safety Act as well as the Highway Safety Act, giving the federal government sweeping new authority to set safety standards. By 1968, seat belts were required in every new car. Despite a massive increase in highway traffic in the last 60 years, far fewer fatalities happen on the road today.

highlights.title: 'Digger' Ending Explained: A Spoiler-Filled Breakdown of Tom Cruise's Wild New Movie
highlights.summary: Digger contains three big reveals that reshape our understanding of the movie in various ways. To really understand what Digger is about, you need to grapple with all three, and the way they fit together (both successfully and unsuccessfully) to tell a complex story about finding meaning at the end…
body: Digger is many things. It’s the first Tom Cruise movie in over a decade not to feature recognizable IP, fighter planes, or both. Its director Alejandro Iñárritu's biggest swing yet after divisive, high-brow films like Birdman and The Revenant. It’s a brutal condemnation of late-stage capitalism. It’s also a pretty clever magic trick.

The first big reveal comes about 30 minutes into Digger. After meeting the aging oil baron Rockwell Digger (Cruise), we quickly learn that his Greenland drilling operation has accidentally dislodged a massive hunk of ice into the Atlantic Ocean, and it’s heading straight for Northern Europe. The U.S. President (John Goodman) and his cabinet show up at Digger’s mansion to discuss their best options (there are none). Then, as Digger and President Compson step aside into a private room to discuss other matters, Iñárritu plays his first trick: The majestic tree outside slowly tips over in front of them… and then a giant hand reaches out from behind the horizon to grab it.

highlights.title: Video Games Europe hits back at EU watchdog targeting King, Supercell, Mojang and more over IAP practices
highlights.summary: The EU’s Consumer Protection Cooperation Network has launched coordinated enforcement actions against games companies including King, Supercell, Mojang, Riot Games, Activision Blizzard and Ubisoft, over how they sell and handle in-game virtual currencies.
body: The CPC Network brings together national consumer protection authorities from across the EU and EEA and is coordinated by the European Commission. In a joint statement published September 30, it said it had found that “a high number of video game companies” had made no substantive changes to their practices since it published non-binding “Key Principles” on in-game currencies in March 2025, despite extensive subsequent talks with industry bodies.

It said the coordinated actions are particularly focused on compliance around variable reward systems such as loot boxes, “dark patterns” and other “harmful influencing techniques”, and practices that directly exhort children to spend money, which it says EU law already prohibits.
Video Games Europe and the European Game Developers Federation pushed back on the CPC Network’s actions in a statement also published on September 30.

highlights.title: New tool lets users repair AI-generated 3D models, then fabricate them just the way they want
highlights.summary: “InstructMesh” can generate designs for everyday objects that are easy to edit and fabricate for both experts and newcomers to 3D modeling.
body: “What you see is what you get” is a guiding principle for many software engineers — create programs where the content you’re editing looks the same as the final product. But when you’re using generative artificial intelligence systems to 3D print, say, a mug, you’ll likely get a cup that can’t hold your coffee. Why is that?

The issue is that AI models understand how an object should look, but not how it works, leading to impractical designs that undermine an item’s intended use. Even if you want to fix these errors, the models are typically hard to edit, especially for users new to 3D design.

Shaw headed over and Yui Hasegawa volleyed wide for the hosts before Ayaka Yamashita had to pull off an excellent stop to deny Irune Dorado as both sides pushed for a winner.

Silvia Cristobal thought she had clinched it in the 89th minute for Real Madrid with a wonderful finish into the top corner - but referee Silvia Gasperotti had whistled to stop play after inadvertently blocking Beth Mead from reaching the ball.

Real Madrid's players and coaching staff were furious and appealed for the goal to stand but ultimately this closely fought contest ended in a draw - the same result City achieved in their opening game away to Bayern Munich last week.

body: The story follows Lowen Ashleigh (Johnson), a struggling writer who gets the opportunity of a lifetime when Jeremy Crawford (Hartnett), the husband of famous author Verity Crawford (Hathaway), offers her the chance to complete Verity’s successful book series.

The offer includes a huge sum of money and new living arrangements in the Crawfords’ stunning, remote Vermont mansion. As the film unfolds, Lowen and Jeremy fall in love, while Verity, paralyzed after a car crash, lives in the same home.

While working on the book, Lowen finds a hidden manuscript in Verity’s office. The text reveals Verity’s darkest secrets, including the fact that she finds no joy in motherhood and resents her twin children, Harper and Crew.
The most shocking part of the manuscript is the revelation that Verity orchestrated the boating accident that resulted in her daughter’s death.

highlights.title: Swing-and-a-miss: MLB rescinds idea to host baseball game in national park after backlash
highlights.summary: Officials in Wyoming had called notion to host game in Grand Teton national park ‘deeply unwelcome’ Major League Baseball (MLB) leadership is no longer considering holding a game inside a national park, according to a letter commissioner Robert Manfred sent to officials in Teton county, Wyoming, on…
body: On 26 September, the Washington Post reported that MLB had reached out to the White House about staging a one-day game at Grand Teton national park in Wyoming. Teton county describes itself as a “a year-round resort community” and sits within the Jackson Hole valley. It’s also a habitat for grizzly bears, osprey, bison and more.

News of MLB’s outreach to the federal government quickly sparked concern about the impact that erecting a field and the infrastructure to hold spectators could have on the natural landscape and habitat of scores of wildlife that call the 310,000-acre (125,500-hectare) park home.

In the letter, Manfred noted that MLB had held games at places like the Fort Bragg military base in North Carolina and the nation’s oldest Negro Leagues stadium in Birmingham, Alabama. He added that MLB staff had been doing their due diligence to see whether a game at Grand Teton was possible and to evaluate the potential environmental impact.
“Since the story was reported, it has become clear that the local community does not want us to continue Grand Teton national park as a potential site,” Manfred wrote.

highlights.title: Google’s new Guided Vision feature can help you read the fine print
highlights.summary: Guided Vision is launching in Gemini Live on compatible Android devices today to use AI to give real-time audio descriptions of anything you point your phone's camera at.
body: People with low vision can use Guided Vision to have Gemini describe what’s nearby and ask follow-up questions.

Like the VoiceOver Live Recognition feature Apple has added to the iPhone and Vision Pro, it’s designed for people who are blind, have low vision, or want assistance in specific situations. In addition to the Gemini app, Guided Vision is also available in Google TalkBack, or users can set up an accessibility shortcut for it in the Settings app on devices running Android 9 and above, after it was announced in a recent set of Pixel updates.

You can also ask follow-up questions about whatever you’re looking at, like asking Gemini to read off the expiration date on an item it helped you find. Google says Gemini will give you audio cues to help line up your camera if you ask about something that’s not in the shot. However, Google cautions users not to rely on Guided Vision for things like “navigation, safe-travel guidance, or obstacle detection,” or as a replacement for a cane or mobility aid.

highlights.title: Venus' mysterious haze is actually cosmic dust
highlights.summary: Venus is shrouded in a veil of mystery. The yellowish “lower haze” at the bottom of its atmosphere was discovered by the Venera and Pioneer Venus probes in the 1970s. These spacecraft were some of the first to successfully send images of the planet back to Earth, but the haze they saw went…
body: What nobody knew then was that the haze is an accumulation of particles from meteorites. “Shooting stars” that burn up in the atmosphere leave behind cosmic dust particles, and after sulfuric acid interacts with these particles, it leaves behind a haze. Planetary scientist Hiroki Karyu and his research team at Tohoku University in Sendai City, Japan, finally figured out how the haze formed using a microphysical model. This type of model involves microphysics —the micro-scale processes that create clouds and precipitation on Earth and other bodies.

“The continuous influx of cosmic dust is sufficient to sustain this lower haze layer with the particle size distribution observed by the entry probes,” Karyu said in a study published in Nature Astronomy. “These haze particles of cosmic origin act as efficient condensation nuclei, promoting cloud formation in the main cloud deck even far from their initial source.”

highlights.title: Judge dismisses antitrust lawsuits over Google’s AI Overviews
highlights.summary: A federal judge has dismissed a pair of antitrust lawsuits filed by Chegg and Rolling Stone parent company Penske Media Corporation, which accused Google of driving away web traffic with its AI-powered search features, as reported earlier by Reuters.
body: Rolling Stone’s parent company and Chegg claimed Google’s AI search features drove away traffic from their sites.

In lawsuits filed last year, Chegg and PMC accused Google of abusing its monopoly power by coercing publishers into supplying content for AI Overviews for free, or risk disappearing from search results. The publishers alleged Google’s practices diverted traffic away from their sites, hurting their revenue.

Judge Mehta, who made a landmark antitrust ruling against Google in 2024, disagrees with Chegg and PMC’s claims. “Plaintiffs have pleaded only that they have an ‘expectation’ that Google will send them search ​traffic if they make their content available for free,” Mehta writes. “But an expectation is not an agreement. It is simply how a general search engine works.”

Mehta adds that the court is not “unsympathetic to the situation publishers now find themselves in,” but writes that antitrust rules can’t replace a legislative body’s decision to address the economic impact of “new innovation.”

highlights.summary: The Fast & Furious films are getting their own television series, with none other than Vin Diesel himself serving as executive producer. As reported by Deadline on October 1, 2026, Peacock has officially given the green light for a Fast & Furious show.
body: Vin Diesel first mentioned the show in May 2026 during a talk at NBCUniversal’s Upfront event, where he explained that fan demand drove Universal Pictures to consider expanding its high-octane IP.

“As you all know, we are very precious about these movies but over the last decade, we’ve realized that the fans have wanted more, they wanted us to expand the legacy characters, their stories,” he said at the event. “And for the last decade, the desire has been for us to enter the TV space.”

Oh and of course, family was part of that decision: “That’s when I knew that the integrity of the characters, the international appeal, what makes us all feel like family will be protected in the TV space,” he added.

Mike Daniels (Sons of Anarchy, PONIES) and Wolfe Coleman (9-1-1: Lone Star) are both writers and co-runners for the show, which is one of four series planned for the Fast & Furious universe. As told by Deadline, one of these shows will be helmed by Nick Wooton (The Endgame) and Charmaine DeGraté (House of the Dragon), while the other two will be handled by Joe Henderson (Lucifer) and Ingrid Escajeda (Griselda).

highlights.title: Europe's CPC targets King, Supercell, Mojang and others over virtual currencies
highlights.summary: Europe's Consumer Protection Cooperation Network is taking "coordinated actions" against a string of top games companies as it looks to investigate compliance with 'Key Principles' on in-game virtual currencies announced last year.
body: The CPC is a network of national authorities responsible for the enforcement of EU consumer protection laws. It has asked Activision Blizzard, Crytek, InnoGames, King, Mojang, Plarium, PLR Worldwide Sales, Riot Games, Supercell and Ubisoft to bring their commercial practices in line relating to in-game virtual currencies.

Games being assessed include Hunt: Showdown 1896, Forge of Empires, Candy Crush Saga, Minecraft, Mech Arena, Gardenscapes, Valorant, Clash of Clans, For Honor, Diablo Immortal and Call of Duty Mobile.

The games were selected for assessment by the CPC Network "in the context of a wide-scale market compliance check due to broad reach, cross-device accessibility, and varied age ratings, all of which amplify the impact of the practices on consumers".
It's not clear what, if any, 'Key Principles' have not been adhered to prior to the CPC Network opening its investigations.

highlights.title: Sarah Jessica Parker’s Gray-Blended Updo is Exquisite
highlights.summary: The actor wore a Simone Rocha sheer gown, along with a matching ribbon in her almost knee-length hair, for a special event at the New York City Ballet.
body: Sarah Jessica Parker is in peak form during ballet season. And tonight, the actor arrived on the red carpet for the New York City Ballet’s Fall Fashion Gala (she’s a founding member of the event) in romantic, ribboned fashion.

For the occasion, Parker chose a floral, sheer gown by Simone Rocha for the occasion, and styled her hair to match. Her long hair—typically worn in beachy waves—was instead pulled back into a Rapunzel-esque updo (extensions helped it reach almost to her knees!). From there, her hairstylist wove a pink ribbon through the hair the perfectly matched those on her gown.

Parker’s longtime colorist, Gina Gilbert at Benjamin Salon, has been working with the star for years to transition her sunny blonde into something gray-friendly. Using a technique called “gray blending,” Gilbert melds bright highlights and natural gray hair into a seamless look.
Parker isn’t the only star who’s stepped out this week with their gray on full display: at the Zurich Film Festival, actor Olivia Colman made a chic case for quitting dye with her silver curls.

highlights.title: SpaceX describes surgical intervention before launch of latest crew mission
highlights.summary: A four-person crew rocketed into orbit Thursday from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, heading for a six-month expedition on the International Space Station.
body: Riding a Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon spacecraft, the four crew members departed from Space Launch Complex-40 at Cape Canaveral at 11:10 am EDT (15:10 UTC) Thursday. Nine minutes later, they were in orbit to begin closing in on the space station for docking Thursday evening.

The launch was delayed from mid-September to replace a balky valve in the Dragon spacecraft’s propulsion system, a task that involved cutting into a propellant line inside the ship to swap out a faulty component.

Jessica Watkins, a 38-year-old geologist turned astronaut, leads the four-person crew sent into orbit Thursday, becoming the first Black woman to command a spacecraft. Watkins is the only veteran astronaut on the mission —designated Crew-13 —after spending 170 days in orbit on a long-duration spaceflight in 2022.

Pilot Luke Delaney, a Marine Corps veteran, was seated next to Watkins for the Dragon spacecraft’s ascent into orbit. Two international crew members rounded out the Crew-13 team: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk, a former pilot in the Royal Canadian Air Force, and Sergey Teteryatnikov, a Russian cosmonaut who served as a naval engineer before his selection to the Roscosmos Cosmonaut Corps in 2021.

highlights.title: The eternal complement
highlights.summary: Advanced AI may matter most for the routine work behind breakthrough ideas. Explore why execution could shape the next economy and the pace of progress.
body: Authors’ note: This is the first essay in our series on the next economy, part of a new platform to host independent voices exploring an AGI future. It reflects our views, not those of OpenAI or our colleagues.

Our equations tell a mostly coherent account of the universe from its first moments. With our telescopes, we have looked to the reaches of the cosmos and glimpsed its early history. We know about the birth of stars and the formation of galaxies.
The explanations we seek span the universe, while our bodies have barely left home. Our minds venture way beyond the reach of our hands.

One possibility is that we needn’t go very far, that the deepest truths might be fathomed from a single planet. Armed with enlightened reasoning and efficient instruments, we reveal the universe without traversing it. In this story, our civilization advances through depth instead of width. It would help explain why we haven’t seen other intelligent life: we might live in a galaxy full of brilliant minds that never needed to expand and become noticeable to us.
points: Advanced AI may matter most for the routine work behind breakthrough ideas.

highlights.title: Viral Short Horror Film Portrait of God Gets Feature Length Movie Starring Chase Infiniti
highlights.summary: Viral internet short film Portrait of God is getting the Hollywood treatment, with Chase Infiniti set to star in a feature length adaptation of the YouTube-famous horror video.
body: If you’re an avid horror fan, chances are you’ve watched Dylan Clark’s viral horror short Portrait of God on YouTube at some point. The seven-and-a-half-minute video centers on college student Mia Reilly as she rehearses a presentation; her topic discusses a mysterious painting — or rather, a photograph of a painting — that, some say, shows a portrait of God.

The photo of said portrait is simply a black image, but testimonies from viewers tell a different story. Reilly says that “some insist they see a person in the darkness,” with subjects claiming in audio recordings that they see a “wrinkled, skinny” man — or at least, something that’s “close to a man.”

I won’t spoil the rest of the short for you, but I highly recommend checking it out if you haven’t seen it yet. Clark packed quite a punch in such a short amount of time, with his video racking up over 10 million views since being uploaded four years ago, and it seems like major studios took notice.

highlights.title: Hacks of 2 federal agencies in a month have spilled a bonanza of sensitive data
highlights.summary: The Pentagon is informing more than 2 million current and former military members that their personnel records storing sensitive personal information were stolen over a monthslong compromise of one of its networks.
body: The records, according to one notification letter posted to Reddit, included Social Security numbers, names, addresses, sex, race, and occupational specialty. This last category could be particularly valuable to foreign adversaries because it could help their intelligence agencies in identifying high-value military personnel. Starting last October, hackers gained access to a system operated by the Defense Manpower Data Center, which collates Department of Defense personnel records. The Pentagon says that the breach compromised the records of 2.8 million living individuals.

The incident is the second time a major network breach in recent months has exposed sensitive US government personnel records that criminal groups or foreign adversaries could use. Last month, the ransomware group ShinyHunters claimed it hacked into FBI systems and stole records of thousands of the agency’s current or former employees. Reuters reported the job titles in the records included ones related to investigating China or Russia.

highlights.title: Gears of War: E-Day Is 100x More Fun Playing Co-op
highlights.summary: Playing solo, Gears of War: E-Day is a perfectly serviceable third-person shooter. Playing with a friend? On the same screen? Gears of War: E-Day is transcendent.
body: This is largely due to the modern gaming landscape, which has seen couch co-op games become as fleetingly rare as other once-common aspects of daily life, like Cava bowls and reading comprehension. Gears of War set the standard for local co-op back in the 2000s. During the Xbox 360 era, couch co-op games were everywhere. Even Insomniac made one. But due to a wide range of factors — shifting player tastes, technological restrictions, balance sheets — developers moved away from the trend. In 2026, Gears of War: E-Day stands out for offering a mode that’s more than just perfunctory. It’s essential.

“Splitscreen, specifically on console, that's core to Gears,” Gears of War brand director Nicole Fawcette told me during an interview at Gamescom 2026. “That's always been the DNA of the game. Like we are… We’ve always been a co-op game.”

highlights.title: Pierpaolo Piccioli presents ‘most personal show’ at Balenciaga
highlights.summary: Italian designer imbues collection with signature flourishes and style rooted in the craft of the couture atelier. It was “the most personal show I have done here”, the designer Pierpaolo Piccioli said after his Balenciaga presentation at Paris fashion week on Thursday.
body: Piccioli, who always wears a coral necklace, placed a monumental sculpture of undersea coral crafted from fabric in the middle of the catwalk. Like Cristóbal Balenciaga, Piccioli is both a maximalist and a minimalist. He likes boldness but not fuss, each look one audacious idea executed cleanly. A floor-length ivory cape fastened with a simple gold clasp. A black suit with one bold slash of tangerine at the jacket hem. A gown covered from neck to ankle in bubbles of organza.

“I like surfaces to be either entirely embellished or super clean,” he said. He loves colour for how instinctively we react to it, because “how you feel in your clothes is much more important than how you look in them”.

A year into the job, Piccioli has his reasons to feel the need to stake Balenciaga’s territory as his own. He used the show to remind the Paris audience that his way of making clothes, which is rooted in the craft of the couture atelier rather than in contemporary obsessions with branding and virality and the attention economy, is what Cristobal himself would have wanted for his house.
